headline: Highest risk is medium: MemMachine’s MCP/networked context can amplify prompt injection and data leakage, while the open-source list itself is non-runnable and low-risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A is a non-runnable awesome-list with no I/O surfaces, so it cannot itself ingest B’s outputs. B exposes an MCP Server and REST/Python SDK, and its tool-use pattern connects users through MemMachine; if A’s content is copied into B, B may treat it as trusted context. The interaction is plausible but not directly documented, so uncertainty stays medium.
conditions: IF A’s text is pasted into B’s conversational context or MCP inputs, THEN prompt-injection risk exists.
IF B parses external text as instructions without provenance checks, THEN attacker-controlled content can steer B.
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to all imported text before sending it to B.
Disable automatic execution of instructions found in retrieved content.
Review B’s MCP inputs for instruction-like strings before use.
Keep A as read-only reference material, not an input source.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has network egress none, so it is not a leakage source. B touches long-term user facts and conversational context and has allowlisted network egress plus MCP/API surfaces, so sensitive context can leave the local boundary in default use. The pair risk is driven by B’s documented behavior; A does not materially reduce it.
conditions: IF B is given sensitive user facts or conversational context, THEN those data may traverse allowlisted egress.
IF B’s MCP/API integrations are enabled, THEN copied context can be transmitted off-box.
mitigations: Restrict B to non-sensitive conversations.
Turn off or narrow B’s allowlist to only required endpoints.
Avoid pasting private notes into B.
Use a separate workspace for any sensitive material.
Review B’s outbound requests for unexpected payloads.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write, network, or mutable-resource surfaces, so it cannot conflict over shared state. B has network egress and MCP/API access, but no filesystem write or git/database scopes are documented. Because the pair lacks overlapping mutable capabilities in the profiles, only a small conflict risk remains if an external orchestrator adds shared state.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives both agents the same mutable resource, THEN write conflicts can occur.
IF B is extended with filesystem or git write access, THEN contention risk increases.
mitigations: Keep A read-only.
Do not grant B shared write access without locking.
Separate B’s API credentials from any other agent.
Document which resources each agent may mutate.
Add a simple mutex in the orchestrator if shared state is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a static resource list, so it does not generate operational facts. B is an agent that can act on conversational context, and its MCP/API surfaces make it plausible that A’s content could be forwarded into B as guidance. Without a verification step, B may over-trust copied recommendations, but the absence of direct action authority keeps this below high.
conditions: IF A’s recommendations are copied into B as authoritative context, THEN B may propagate errors.
IF B is configured to act on unverified travel advice, THEN downstream mistakes can cascade.
mitigations: Require B to cite source URLs before acting.
Insert a human review step for any travel action.
Mark A-derived content as unverified reference only.
Disable auto-execution of B outputs for bookings or messages.
Compare B’s output against a second source before use.

E_compliance.rationale: A is an open-source reference list with no touched data classes, so it presents no residency or retention issue. B touches long-term user facts and conversational context, but the profile does not show regulated data classes, residency mismatch, or special certifications. With only docs-level evidence, the compliance concern is limited to ordinary retention/handling gaps.
conditions: IF B is used to store personal preferences beyond the session, THEN retention policy review is needed.
IF regulated personal data is entered into B, THEN a separate compliance assessment is required.
mitigations: Avoid entering regulated data into B.
Publish a short retention notice for B.
Delete stale conversational context regularly.
Confirm where B stores memory data.
Use a separate instance for any regulated workflow.
